May 2024: stepping back from executive management

On Tuesday, 21 May 2024, the [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]] confirmed that its founder Klaus Schwab was moving away from day-to-day management of the organization after more than 50 years at the helm.[{n}] The Forum described the change as part of a multiyear strategy shifting governance to a president and managing board — [[borge-brende|Børge Brende]] was then president — and said Schwab would transition to chairman of the board of trustees, with the board organized around four strategic committees.[{n}] No successor was named to become the face of the Forum's annual Davos meeting.[{n}]

Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] observed that Schwab had run the WEF since 1971 and grown it into 'the pinnacle of the Global World Order,' and called the timing of his departure notable.[{n}] Her questions were 'why now' questions: why step down when the vision was said to be near completion, whether the choice was his, how the timing affected key programs, and who was actually calling the shots at the WEF.[{n}]

On 21 May 2024 the Forum confirmed that founder [[klaus-schwab|Klaus Schwab]] was stepping back from day-to-day management after more than 50 years, moving to the role of chairman of the board of trustees.[{n}] In a statement to CNBC, the Forum said that 'since 2015, the World Economic Forum has been transforming from a convening platform to the leading global institution for public-private cooperation,' and that the organization had been undergoing 'a planned governance evolution from a founder-managed organization to one where a President and Managing Board assume full executive responsibility.'[{n}] [[borge-brende|Børge Brende]] was president at the time, and the trustee board was to be organized around four strategic committees; no successor as public face of the Davos meeting was announced.[{n}]

Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] argued that through the WEF's change network the global governors drive their agenda through every institution, sector and geography, and recalled the preceding Davos meeting where the energy and rhetoric had shifted and [[kevin-roberts|Kevin Roberts]] of the [[heritage-foundation|Heritage Foundation]] told attendees, 'It's laughable that you or anyone would describe Davos as protecting liberal democracy.'[{n}] She concluded: 'The invisible hand is no longer invisible.'[{n}]
President of the WEF during the 2024 transition

At the time of [[klaus-schwab|Klaus Schwab]]'s May 2024 step-back from day-to-day management, Brende was president of the [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]], the office to which — alongside a managing board — full executive responsibility was being shifted under the Forum's planned governance evolution.[{n}]

Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] recalled Roberts, head of the [[heritage-foundation|Heritage Foundation]], scolding attendees at a [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]] meeting in Davos and telling them, 'It's laughable that you or anyone would describe Davos as protecting liberal democracy.'[{n}] She cited the episode as a marker that the rhetoric and energy around Davos had changed.[{n}]

Heritage Foundation president [[kevin-roberts|Kevin Roberts]] publicly rebuked attendees at a [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]] Davos meeting, telling them it was 'laughable' to describe Davos as protecting liberal democracy — an exchange cited in Badlands commentary as evidence of shifting elite dynamics ahead of [[klaus-schwab|Klaus Schwab]]'s 2024 departure from executive management.[{n}]
